title: Bug: excessive debug logging in parse_routes_process() causes 10+ Gig log files in T2 topologies
author: vhlushko-cisco
body:
### Is it platform specific

generic

### Importance or Severity

High

### Description of the bug

When you run these BGP tests on the T2 topology device
```
bgp/test_traffic_shift.py
bgp/test_seq_idf_isolation.py
bgp/test_startup_tsa_tsb_service.py
bgp/reliable_tsa/test_reliable_tsa_stable.py
bgp/reliable_tsa/test_reliable_tsa_flaky.py
```
you may notice that the log files produced by these test has an enormous size, individual log file could be 10+ Gigs.

The root cause of the excessive logs:

```
sonic@sonic-server:~/test_logs/23341_nightly/bgp/reliable_tsa$ head -n 5700 test_reliable_tsa_flaky_2025-04-11-08-35-32.log |less
11/04/2025 21:18:01 parallel.parallel_run                    L0153 DEBUG  | Started process 13915 running target "parse_routes_process--<EosHost VM0106>"
11/04/2025 21:18:01 base._run                                L0071 DEBUG  | /data/tests/bgp/route_checker.py::parse_routes_process#104: [VM0105] AnsibleModule::eos_command, args=[], kwargs={"commands": ["show ip bgp neighbors 10.0.0.20 received-routes detail | grep -E \"BGP routing table entry for |Community: \
""], "module_ignore_errors": true}
11/04/2025 21:18:01 base._run                                L0071 DEBUG  | /data/tests/bgp/route_checker.py::parse_routes_process#104: [VM0103] AnsibleModule::eos_command, args=[], kwargs={"commands": ["show ip bgp neighbors 10.0.0.12 received-routes detail | grep -E \"BGP routing table entry for |Community: \""], "module_ignore_errors": true}
11/04/2025 21:18:01 base._run                                L0071 DEBUG  | /data/tests/bgp/route_checker.py::parse_routes_process#104: [VM0106] AnsibleModule::eos_command, args=[], kwargs={"commands": ["show ip bgp neighbors 10.0.0.32 received-routes detail | grep -E \"BGP routing table entry for |Community: \
""], "module_ignore_errors": true}
11/04/2025 21:18:03 base._run                                L0108 DEBUG  | /data/tests/bgp/route_checker.py::parse_routes_process#104: [VM0107] AnsibleModule::eos_command Result => {"changed": false, "stdout": ["BGP routing table entry for 10.1.0.1/32\nBGP routing table entry for 10.1.0.2/32\nBGP routing table
 entry for 10.1.0.3/32\nBGP routing table entry for 100.1.0.33/32\n      Community: 5060:12345\nBGP routing table entry for 100.1.0.35/32\n      Community: 5060:12345\nBGP routing table entry for 100.1.0.37/32\n      Community: 5060:12345\nBGP routing table entry for 100.1.0.39/32\n      Community: 5060:12345\n
BGP routing table entry for 100.1.0.41/32\n      Community: 5060:12345\nBGP routing table entry for 100.1.0.43/32\n      Community: 5060:12345\nBGP routing table entry for 100.1.0.45/32\n      Community: 5060:12345\nBGP routing table entry for 100.1.0.47/32\n      Community: 5060:12345\nBGP routing table entry for 100.1.0.49/32\n      Community: 5060:12345\nBGP routing table entry for 100.1.0.50/32\n      Community: 5060:12345\nBGP routing table entry for 100.1.0.51/32\n      Community: 5060:12345\nBGP routing table entry for 100.1.0.52/32\n      Community: 5060:12345\nBGP routing table entry for 100.1.0.53/32\
````

the [sonic-mgmt/tests/bgp/route_checker.py::parse_routes_process#104](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/blob/a7c41d976c33ee99bb0b3a19f831daecaa95bde3/tests/bgp/route_checker.py#L104) printing the received routes (the output of received routes for one VM is very large) for every ARISTA VM BGP neighbor, the output is very large - 10+ Gigs.

Why it is so large for T2 topology:

- There are 72 BGP neighbors.

- There are 10 testcases in the bgp/reliable_tsa/test_reliable_tsa_flaky.py.

- For every testcase the `verify_route_on_neighbors_when_duts_on_tsb` function is called which is using the `bgp/route_checker.py::parse_routes_process#104` function for the IPv4 and IPv6 routes.

- The `verify_route_on_neighbors_when_duts_on_tsb` also called for every linecard.


I’ve calculated, there are 52 calls of bgp/route_checker.py::parse_routes_process#104 only for one BGP neighbor VM0100:

```
sonic@sonic-server:~/test_logs/23341_nightly/bgp/reliable_tsa$ rg -e "Started process .* running target \"parse_routes_process--<EosHost VM0100>\"" test_reliable_tsa_flaky_2025-04-11-08-35-32.log |wc -l
52
```

### Steps to Reproduce

Run one of these testcases and check the log file size.
```
bgp/test_traffic_shift.py
bgp/test_seq_idf_isolation.py
bgp/test_startup_tsa_tsb_service.py
bgp/reliable_tsa/test_reliable_tsa_stable.py
bgp/reliable_tsa/test_reliable_tsa_flaky.py
```


### Actual Behavior and Expected Behavior

The log files shout not be 10+ Gigs.

linkedPullRequests.title: [bgp] Suppress verbose logging in route_checker to prevent 10+ GB log files
linkedPullRequests.author: sonicly1g
linkedPullRequests.body:
**Summary:**
This PR fixes excessive debug logging in `route_checker.py` that produces 10+ GB log files on T2 topologies, filling disks and slowing down test infrastructure.

**Context:** The `parse_routes_process()` and `parse_routes_process_vsonic()` functions call `eos_command()` and `shell()` with the default `verbose=True`. The Ansible debug logger then dumps both the full command arguments AND the complete results (thousands of BGP routing table entries per neighbor) into the log file. On T2 topologies with many VMs and large routing tables, this produces individual log files exceeding 10 GB.

**Fix:** Pass `verbose=False` to the `eos_command()` and `shell()` calls in the route parsing functions. This follows the existing pattern used by `parse_rib()` in `bgp_helpers.py` which already uses `verbose=False` for the same reason. Route data is parsed programmatically — there is no diagnostic value in logging the raw output. Errors are still properly reported via `pytest_assert`.

Fixes #19165

### Type of change
- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Testbed and Framework(new/improvement)
- [ ] New Test case
- [ ] Test case improvement

### Back port request
- [ ] 202205
- [ ] 202305
- [ ] 202311
- [ ] 202405
- [ ] 202411
- [ ] 202505
- [ ] 202511

### Approach
#### What is the motivation for this PR?
To prevent test log files from growing to 10+ GB, which fills disks and degrades test infrastructure on T2 topologies.

#### How did you do it?
Added `verbose=False` to three call sites in `tests/bgp/route_checker.py`:
1. `host.eos_command(commands=[cmd], module_ignore_errors=True, verbose=False)` — primary route query
2. `host.eos_command(commands=[cmd_backup], module_ignore_errors=True, verbose=False)` — fallback route query  
3. `host.shell(bgp_nbr_cmd, verbose=False)` — vsonic route query

This matches the existing pattern in `parse_rib()` (`bgp_helpers.py:183`) which already uses `verbose=False`.

#### How did you verify/test it?
- Code review confirmed that `verbose=False` suppresses the DEBUG-level logging of command arguments and results in `AnsibleHostBase._run()` (`tests/common/devices/base.py:73-89, 119-128`)
- The `verbose=False` parameter is an established pattern already used in `parse_rib()` for the same reason
- Error handling via `pytest_assert` and `res['failed']` checks remains unchanged

#### Any platform specific information?
Most impactful on T2 topologies with many BGP neighbors, but the fix is generic.

#### Supported testbed topology if it is a new test case?
N/A — existing infrastructure fix.

### Documentation
N/A

comments.author: rustiqly
comments.body:
## Log Size Analysis

**Source:** Issue #19165 provides concrete data from T2 topology test runs.

**Before (verbose=True, current master):**
- Each `eos_command` result dumps the full received-routes table for every BGP neighbor
- T2 topology: **72 BGP neighbors**, each with hundreds of routes
- Single `parse_routes_process` call: dumps route tables for all neighbors × both IPv4 and IPv6
- These functions are called **multiple times per test** (e.g., `check_and_log_routes_diff` runs before/after TSA/TSB transitions)
- Result: **10+ GB per test log file** (confirmed in #19165)

**After (verbose=False):**
- Only the Ansible module call + kwargs are logged (the command being run) — a few hundred bytes per call
- Route data is still parsed programmatically and validated via `pytest_assert`
- Failures still produce diagnostic output (assertion messages include which routes are missing)
- Estimated log size: **< 100 MB** for the same test suite (normal pytest output + ansible call metadata)

**Reduction: ~99%** (10+ GB → < 100 MB)

The `verbose=False` parameter only suppresses the `Result =>` debug line that dumps the full stdout/stderr of the Ansible module call. It does not affect error handling or test assertions.
